title: Etale paths transport finite and lisse adic fibre functors
statement:
Let $Y$ be a connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-scheme] and let $\bar y,\bar z$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $F_{\bar y},F_{\bar z}$ denote the fibre functors on finite locally constant sheaves of sets, and put $\pi_y=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ and $\pi_z=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar z})$, with the profinite topologies of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. There exists a natural isomorphism $t:F_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar z}$. Every such $t$ induces an isomorphism of topological groups
$$c_t:\pi_y\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_z,\qquad g\longmapsto tgt^{-1}.$$
For two such isomorphisms $t,t'$, the element $a=t't^{-1}$ belongs to $\pi_z$ and $c_{t'}=\operatorname{Int}(a)c_t$.

For a finite ring $A$, evaluation of $t$ on the underlying finite locally constant sheaf of a lisse $A$-module sheaf gives an $A$-linear isomorphism of stalks, natural in the module sheaf; the action on these stalks is that of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1). It commutes with maps of finite coefficient rings and with composition of paths.

Suppose in addition that $Y$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact) and separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, pqf-def-locnoeth] and that a prime $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$. Use the lisse $\mathcal O_E$-, $E$- and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaves, their scalar extensions and fibres of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite inside the fixed algebraic closure. The finite-level maps of $t$ induce natural linear isomorphisms $t_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_{\bar z}$ at each of these coefficient levels. They commute with scalar extension, identity paths and composition of paths, and satisfy
$$t_{\mathcal F}\rho_{\bar y}(g)t_{\mathcal F}^{-1}=\rho_{\bar z}(c_t(g)),\qquad (t')_{\mathcal F}=\rho_{\bar z}(a)t_{\mathcal F},$$
where the two stalk actions are those of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2).

source.place: Stacks Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (2), via Tag 0BN5, lemma-functoriality-galois; finite-module and adic extension of this transport using literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf (1.1.1) b)-d), pp.146-147

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$. By [thm-galois-fundamental], evaluation at $\bar y$ is an equivalence $B:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal C_{\pi_y}$ whose underlying-set functor is $F_{\bar y}$. Choose a quasi-inverse $Q$ with counit $\epsilon:QB\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$. The functor $F_{\bar z}$ is finite-valued and exact: [lem-fet-galois-category] says this on finite etale covers by the axioms of [def-galois-category], and [thm-galois-lc-etale] identifies that fibre functor with the one on $\mathcal C$. Equivalences, including $Q$, preserve finite limits and colimits by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits]. Thus $H=F_{\bar z}Q:\mathcal C_{\pi_y}\to\mathbf{Sets}$ is exact and finite-valued.

source.place: Theorem 0BND (1); Lemma 0BN5, reduction to finite group sets

proof.text:
Apply [lem-wf-exact-finite-gsets-forgetful] with $G=\pi_y$ to obtain $s:U\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. Define
$$t_{\mathcal S}=F_{\bar z}(\epsilon_{\mathcal S})\circ s_{B\mathcal S}:F_{\bar y}(\mathcal S)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar z}(\mathcal S).$$
The identification $UB=F_{\bar y}$ is that in [thm-galois-fundamental]. Naturality of $s$ and $\epsilon$ proves naturality of $t$, and both factors are bijective. This proves existence without choosing points separately in the different stalks.

source.place: Lemma 0BN5, first sentence of proof, using Lemma 0BMV; Theorem 0BND (2)

proof.text:
Now fix any natural isomorphism $t$. Composition gives a natural automorphism $c_t(g)=tgt^{-1}$ of $F_{\bar z}$. It preserves products in the group, and $c_{t^{-1}}$ is its inverse. To check continuity use the topology in [def-galois-fibre-functor] on a common small skeleton of $\mathcal C$. At an object $\mathcal S$ the target evaluation is
$$g\longmapsto t_{\mathcal S}g_{\mathcal S}t_{\mathcal S}^{-1}.$$
It factors through source evaluation into a finite discrete permutation group, followed by conjugation between finite discrete permutation groups. It is continuous, so the map into the product and its induced-subspace factor $c_t$ are continuous. The same calculation with $t^{-1}$ proves continuity of its inverse. Also $a=t't^{-1}$ is a natural automorphism of $F_{\bar z}$ and
$$t'gt'^{-1}=(t't^{-1})(tgt^{-1})(tt'^{-1})=a\,c_t(g)\,a^{-1}.$$
This proves the asserted topological isomorphism and change-of-path formula.

source.place: Lemma 0BN5, transport of structure and inner-conjugation assertions, with topology calculation written out

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse finite $A$-module sheaf. Its underlying sheaf and its square are finite locally constant. Naturality of $t$ with respect to the two projections forces $t_{\mathcal F\times\mathcal F}=(t_{\mathcal F},t_{\mathcal F})$ under the stalk product identifications. Applying naturality to addition and to each set-sheaf map $x\mapsto ax$ gives
$$t_{\mathcal F}(x+x')=t_{\mathcal F}(x)+t_{\mathcal F}(x'),\qquad t_{\mathcal F}(ax)=a\,t_{\mathcal F}(x).$$
Thus $t_{\mathcal F}$ is an $A$-linear bijection; naturality for module maps follows from naturality for their underlying set maps. The same construction applies to $t^{-1}$. By [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1), evaluating a loop $g$ on this underlying sheaf is precisely its stipulated stalk action. Evaluating an identity or a composite of paths gives the identity or composite linear map, component by component.

source.place: Theorem 0BND (2), extension to module structures by naturality

proof.text:
For a finite-ring homomorphism $A\to A'$ put $\mathcal F'=A'\otimes_A\mathcal F$. The lissity and stalk identifications, including their pure-tensor formulas, are [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension](3). For each $b\in A'$ the map of underlying set sheaves $i_b:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, $x\mapsto b\otimes x$, is available to naturality of $t$; it need not be $A$-linear. Hence
$$t_{\mathcal F'}(b\otimes x)=b\otimes t_{\mathcal F}(x).$$
Additivity extends this equality to sums of pure tensors, which generate scalar extension. This is the asserted coefficient compatibility, including noncommutative finite rings. For two successive coefficient maps both composites send $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $cb\otimes t_{\mathcal F}(x)$, so the coefficient comparisons are coherent. Identity and composite paths satisfy the same equality.

source.place: Finite scalar extension: naturality and the stalk scalar-extension formula; Stacks sites-modules lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text:
Assume now the additional Noetherian, separated and invertibility hypotheses, exactly as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. For an integral lisse system $\mathcal F=(\mathcal F_n)$ put
$$T_{\mathcal F}((x_n)_n)=(t_{\mathcal F_n}(x_n))_n.$$
The transition maps are maps of underlying finite locally constant set sheaves, even though their coefficient rings vary. Naturality of $t$ therefore makes the displayed family compatible. The same construction using $t^{-1}$ is inverse to it. Scalar multiplication by $b\in\mathcal O_E$ reduces to multiplication by its image in each $A_{E,n}$, so the finite-level linearity proves $\mathcal O_E$-linearity. For a compatible family $u_n$, naturality is the equality $t_{\mathcal G_n}(u_nx_n)=u_n(t_{\mathcal F_n}x_n)$ at every $n$. The integral fibre and its maps are precisely the inverse-limit functor of [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors](1). Identities and composition of paths hold at every coordinate, hence on the inverse limit.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b), p.146: compatible finite-level systems and their fibres

proof.text: For $E\subset L$ use the scalar extension prescribed in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](3). Its level $m$ is $\mathcal F_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,m}$, with $n=\lceil m/e\rceil$ and $e$ the ramification index. The finite scalar formula proved above identifies its path map with $1\otimes t_{\mathcal F_n}$. The fibre scalar comparisons at both geometric points are the ones supplied by [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2). To check their compatibility with path maps, project the extended integral fibre to its level $m$: on a pure tensor $b\otimes(x_j)_j$ both routes give $b\otimes t_{\mathcal F_n}(x_n)$. Additivity gives equality on the whole scalar-extended module, and equality of every inverse-limit coordinate proves equality of the maps. For successive extensions this calculation again gives the same iterated pure tensor, independently of the reindexing. Thus the integral path maps commute with scalar extension, including ramified extensions.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b), d), pp.146-147: finite-level coefficient extensions

proof.text: For a lisse $E$-sheaf represented by $\mathcal F\otimes E$, define its path map to be $T_{\mathcal F}\otimes1_E$. A rational morphism is a finite sum of tensors $a\otimes u$ in the Hom module of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](2). The fibre functor sends this to the same linear combination of the integral fibre maps by [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors](2). Integral naturality therefore implies naturality for every rational morphism, including rational isomorphisms between different integral models. This makes the construction independent of any presentation up to its canonical isomorphism. It is an $E$-linear isomorphism, its inverse is the rationalized map for $t^{-1}$, and identities, composition of paths and scalar extension follow by tensoring the already proved equalities.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) c), p.147: rationalized Hom spaces

proof.text:
For a model $(E,\mathcal F)$ of a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf, define
$$t_{(E,\mathcal F)}=t_{\mathcal F}\otimes1_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}.$$
By [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](4), a morphism of models is represented over a common finite extension $L$; the algebraic fibre functor is scalar extension of the rational one by [def-pod-lisse-adic-fibre-functors](3). The finite-extension compatibility just proved identifies the two model path maps with their extensions to $L$. Rational naturality over $L$ gives the required square. Passing to a larger common field preserves that equality, so it descends to the colimit Hom space. The same argument proves compatibility with scalar extension and composition, and the inverse is induced by $t^{-1}$. This proves all the asserted functorialities at the algebraic coefficient level.

For a finite lisse module sheaf evaluate the equality $c_t(g)=tgt^{-1}$ at its underlying set sheaf. By the evaluation-action description in [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) this gives
$$t_{\mathcal F}\rho_{\bar y}(g)t_{\mathcal F}^{-1}=\rho_{\bar z}(c_t(g)).$$
Likewise $t'=a t$ evaluates to $(t')_{\mathcal F}=\rho_{\bar z}(a)t_{\mathcal F}$. Part (2) of that node specifies the integral actions by the finite-level actions and the rational and algebraic actions by their coefficient extensions. Apply these finite equalities at every level, then to the inverse-limit tuples, and then tensor with $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Each operation preserves equality of maps and their composites. The resulting identities are exactly the two displayed adic identities of the statement, with the conjugating element in $\pi_z$.
